precepts.text: Israel was delivered for a spoil, unto captivity, unto death, and for a proverb of reproach to all the nations among whom we are dispersed.
precepts.point: The majority of the masses did not have what we call the Old Testament. It was the learned men that had the parchments, and it was their job to instruct the people. But now God gave it to the apostles to teach.

precepts.why:
Tobit shows the dispersed are Israel once again: “For they obeyed not thy commandments: wherefore thou hast delivered us for a spoil, and unto captivity, and unto death, and for a proverb of reproach to all the nations among whom we are dispersed.”

Israel disobeyed the commandments, and so was delivered for a spoil, into captivity, unto death, and made a proverb of reproach among all the nations where they were dispersed. The Pharisees understood Tobit and the dispersed, just as they understood Isaiah 11. That is why they said of Christ, “will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?” They knew who the dispersed were.

moments.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: Sarah the daughter of Raguel had been married to seven husbands whom Asmodeus killed before they had lain with her; they were her husbands by espousal, before any consummation, and her father's maids taunted her for it.
She was the only daughter of her father, who had no child to be his heir and no near kinsman; she had no one to keep herself for to hold her father's inheritance.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: The prayers of them both were heard, and Raphael was sent to heal Tobit's eyes and to give Sarah to Tobias, because she belonged to Tobias by right of inheritance.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: Sara the daughter of Raguel was also reproached by her father's maids: why?
Because that she had been married to seven husbands, whom Asmodeus the evil spirit had killed: the demon had killed.

Before they had lain with her: whoa, whoa, whoa. When? Before what? Before they had sex, they were called her what? Husbands. She was a wife and they were husbands before they did what? Lain with her. Before they had sex. What are we reading? The Bible.
Dost thou not know, said they, that thou hast strangled thine husbands: thine what? Thine husbands.

Neither wast thou named after any of them: guess what? They weren't confused. Raguel, he wasn't confused. Sarah wasn't confused. She had seven husbands. She didn't have sex with none of them, but each and every one of them was called her husband. And she was the wife to all seven of them. They weren't confused. That's not a coincidence that it says before they lain with her, or before they had sex with her, before they consummated the marriage.
